significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that subliminally transferred and overtly induced misalignment share a causal low-dimensional mechanism: the student's changes "concentrate along the same single linear 'misalignment direction'" and removing it eliminates the transmitted behavior while preserving capability. This is a form-(ii) causal claim—essentially direction, causal role, and ablation repair—rather than a scaling law or transferable quantitative relation, so it fixes whether one defense and mechanistic explanation covers both phenomena but remains bounded to misalignment; it establishes both a transfer phenomenon and its proposed mechanism. Cloud et al.'s "Subliminal Learning" and Betley et al.'s "Emergent Misalignment" make the negative branch informative: failure of direction reuse would rule out a shared-mechanism account and imply, as the claim says, that "covert channels require their own detection and mitigation"; true and false therefore denote clear, consequential alternatives. In the topic-substitution check, merely proposing to extend subliminal learning would not earn this score—the specific shared-direction and causal-ablation conclusion supplies the above-median increment, though its standard single-behavior causal form caps it at 6.

reach.justification: The concrete handles are projection onto the "pre-identified emergent-misalignment direction" as a diagnostic and "ablating that direction from the student after subliminal finetuning" as an intervention that auditors of distillation pipelines could apply. These are primarily post-hoc to trait acquisition, although ablation could occur before deployment; the claim does not forecast corruption before training or data ingestion. After recalibration on a new model, the conclusion supplies a procedure for finding and removing a direction but no asserted scaling, threshold, or quantitative relation predicting what the new model's geometry will be, and the stated risks acknowledge dependence on the "specific teacher's misalignment flavor" and possible model specificity. The topic-substitution check lowers the reach of subliminal-learning research alone below 5; this claim earns 6 because it hands auditors a deployable diagnostic-and-mitigation target, but its unstated cross-family scope and per-model rediscovery prevent the 7–8 band.
